issue_context.title: AIP-81 Implement DAG Report Endpoint in REST API (FastAPI)
issue_context.body:
### Description

Create an endpoint in FastAPI that returns the DAG report (`dagbag.dagbag_stats`).

### Related issues

[AIP-81](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW/AIP-81+Enhanced+Security+in+CLI+via+Integration+of+API)

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [ ] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
comments: Hi @bugraoz93, I can work on this issue, could you assign to me ? Thanks !

review_comments:
Do we need the `subdir` granularity ?

Otherwise in the fastapi application we already have access to the DagBag that is built based on  `DAGS_FOLDER` coming from the configuration file. (`request.app.state.dag_bag`) Also that feels sensitive, because we will be manipulating a user provided path on the server... (for instance provide a path to a really big folder, or something with a lot of zipped archives, such as logs, and the server will spend a lot of time doing unnecessary work => DOS)
Or at least we need to check that the provided path is a subpath of `DAGS_FOLDER`

Hi @pierrejeambrun ,
I agree with reusing `request.app.state.dag_bag` instead of creating a new `DagBag` instance at the router each time. I just tried retrieving `dagbag_stats` from `request.app.state.dag_bag` and found that the `DagBag` for the REST API is constructed with `read_dags_from_db=True`.
https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/airflow/www/extensions/init_dagbag.py#L29
 This means the only way to get a list of DAGs is by calling `collect_dags_from_db`.
 https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/airflow/models/dagbag.py#L596-L605
 
 Additionally, for the `dagbag_stats` information required by this API — such as `file_parse_duration`, `dag_num`, `task_num`, and `warning_num`— these details aren't available in `SerializedDagModel`.  

It seems this would require more effort to sync these additional `dagbag_stats` details from the filesystem to the database. This would involve adding more fields to `SerializedDagModel` and implementing the corresponding sync logic in `DagBag`. 

Is there an alternative solution to retrieve these `dagbag_stats` from the database instead of the filesystem ? Or would implementing this logic for the feature be considered acceptable ?

If we need dags from the filesystem to get that extra information then I don't mind re-creating it. Mayba a small comment there could help. I don't know a better way of achieving that. 

Also you need the `subdir` param so you cannot really re-use the existing dag bag.

> Or at least we need to check that the provided path is a subpath of DAGS_FOLDER

This should be enough in that case I think from a security point of view to not allow arbitrary file system exploration and processing.
